Install development dependences devtools::install_dev_deps(), make sure package passes R CMD check running devtools::check(). R CMD check doesn’t pass cleanly, ’s good idea ask help continuing. title: Chart types
text: visit appears , last shopping step reached (name). Bars, columns, cylinders slices show 100 visits ended (y). Bars columns start zero; polar columns arrange quantities around circle. funnel counts everyone reached step: 100 viewed products, 66 added cart, 42 started checkout 24 purchased. variable-width columns variable-radius slices, z illustrative average session duration minutes, available four steps. Variwide uses column width; variable pie uses radius, zero lower bound. treemap packed bubbles split stage acquisition source. word cloud compares stage source totals.

# fmt: skip shopping <- tibble::tribble( ~name, ~y, ~z, "Viewed", 34, 2.5, "Added", 24, 6, "Checkout", 18, 9, "Purchased", 24, 8 ) # fmt: skip shopping_sources <- tibble::tribble( ~stage, ~source, ~value, "Viewed", "Search", 18, "Viewed", "Social", 10, "Viewed", "Direct", 6, "Added", "Search", 13, "Added", "Social", 7, "Added", "Direct", 4, "Checkout", "Search", 9, "Checkout", "Social", 6, "Checkout", "Direct", 3, "Purchased","Search", 12, "Purchased","Social", 8, "Purchased","Direct", 4 ) gallery( c( "bar", "column", "cylinder", "columnpyramid", "variwide", "polar column", "pie", "variablepie", "lollipop", "dotplot", "item", "waterfall", "packedbubble", "treemap", "wordcloud", "funnel", "pyramid", "funnel3d", "pyramid3d" ), function(label) { type <- sub("^polar ", "", label) points <- shopping if (type %in% c("funnel", "pyramid", "funnel3d", "pyramid3d")) { points$y <- rev(cumsum(rev(points$y))) } if (type == "packedbubble") { return(hchart( shopping_sources, type, hcaes(group = stage, name = source, value = value), minSize = "16%", maxSize = "49%", zMin = 0, layoutAlgorithm = list(splitSeries = TRUE, seriesInteraction = FALSE), dataLabels = list( enabled = TRUE, format = "{point.name}", style = list(fontSize = "9px") ), tooltip = list( pointFormat = "{series.name} / {point.name}: {point.value} visits" ) )) } if (type == "treemap") { nodes <- bind_rows( transmute(shopping, id = name, name), transmute( shopping_sources, id = paste(stage, source, sep = "-"), parent = stage, name = source, value ) ) return(hchart( nodes, type, levels = list( list( level rotation = list(from = 0, to = 0) )) } hchart(points, type, name = "Visits", colorByPoint = TRUE) |> hc_plotOptions( pie = list(dataLabels = list(distance = 8)), variablepie = list( zMin = 0, dataLabels = list(distance = 8), tooltip = list( pointFormat = "{point.name}: {point.y} visits
Average session: {point.z} min" ) ), variwide = list( tooltip = list( pointFormat = "{point.name}: {point.y} visits
Average session: {point.z} min" ) ) ) |> hc_xAxis( categories = points$name, labels = if (startsWith(label, "polar")) { list(distance = 5, style = list(fontSize = "10px")) } ) |> hc_chart( type = type, polar = startsWith(label, "polar"), options3d = list( enabled = type %in% c("cylinder", "funnel3d", "pyramid3d"), alpha = 12, beta = 15 ) ) } )

text: chart data, data can come different ways: numeric character vectors, time series objects, etc. common object data data frame. , ’ll show chart type object highcharter. Highcharter two main functions create chart data another add data existing highchart object. hchart(): generic function take object (like vector, time series, data frames, likert object, etc) return highchart object (chart) hc_add_series(): generic function add data existing highchart object depending type (class) data. last function useful chart data data frame. functions hcaes define aesthetic mappings. 3 functions inspired ggplot2 package. : hchart() works like ggplot2’s qplot. hc_add_series() works like ggplot2’s geom_s. hcaes() works like ggplot2’s aes. main differences ggplot2 need data aesthetics explicit every highcharts functions. First, show data work . general ’ll use structure get chart: <data.frame> data chart. <type_of_chart> string specify type chart. value can : line, spline, area, heatmap, treemap, etc. <aesthetics> mapping use plot. ... parameters configure chart. , basic example :

text: Fit local regression compute predictions standard errors: case ’ll chart original data first store variable called hc (highcharts): can add series chart (like layers ggplot world) using function hc_add_series. parameters functions similar hchart: case add 2 groups series. 1st add spline arearange. ’ll use hc_add_series 2 times.
code: modlss <- loess(dist ~ speed, data = cars) prediction <- predict(modlss, se = TRUE) fit <- mutate(cars, .fitted = prediction$fit, .se = prediction$se.fit) |> arrange(speed) head(fit) ## speed dist .fitted .se ## 1 4 2 5.893628 9.885466 ## 2 4 10 5.893628 9.885466 ## 3 7 4 12.499786 4.990827 ## 4 7 22 12.499786 4.990827 ## 5 8 16 15.281082 4.545284 ## 6 9 10 18.446568 4.308639 hc <- hchart( cars, type = "scatter", hcaes(x = speed, y = dist), name = "Observed distance", showInLegend = TRUE ) hc hc_add_series(, , , hcaes(), ...) # or with the pipe: |> hc_add_series(, , hcaes(), ...) qtint <- qt(0.975, prediction$df) hc |> hc_add_series( fit, type = "spline", hcaes(x = speed, y = .fitted), name = "LOESS fit", id = "fit", # this is for link the arearange series to this one and have one legend lineWidth = 1, showInLegend = TRUE ) |> hc_add_series( fit, type = "arearange", name = "95% confidence interval", hcaes(x = speed, low = .fitted - qtint * .se, high = .fitted + qtint * .se), linkedTo = "fit", # here we link the legends in one. showInLegend = FALSE, color = hex_to_rgba("gray", 0.2), # put a semi transparent color zIndex = -3, # Keep the band behind the observations. tooltip = list( pointFormat = '{series.name}{point.low:.1f}–{point.high:.1f} ft' ) ) |> hc_tooltip( table = TRUE, headerFormat = "Speed: {point.x} mph", valueDecimals = 1, valueSuffix = " ft", style = list(fontFamily = "IBM Plex Sans") )

title: From data to charts
text: data come World Bank’s World Development Indicators. Run following code fetch original JSON responses, join economy map identifiers, choose common year calculate trade measures. Every run downloads data requires internet. six indicators measure population, life expectancy, GDP per person purchasing-power parity (constant 2021 international dollars), urban population, merchandise exports imports (current US dollars). Export histories start 2005. Economies must complete indicators common year, positive income, population trade flows, map match complete export history. latest recent year least 150 complete economies selected checking history. Missing values imputed years mixed. selected year 2024, 179 economies covering 97.6% world population. observation represents economy, rather regional aggregate. World Bank can revise historical observations; metadata$indicators metadata$source_updated record indicator codes source update dates. Trade per person divides flow population. signed balance 100 * (exports - imports) / (exports + imports); can negative, map uses linear, diverging color scale. Export changes include price exchange-rate effects flows nominal.
code: fetch_wdi <- function(path) {   url <- paste0("https://api.worldbank.org/v2/", path)   temp <- tempfile(fileext = ".json")   on.exit(unlink(temp), add = TRUE)   utils::download.file(     url,     temp,     method = "libcurl",     mode = "wb",     quiet = TRUE,     headers = c("User-Agent" = "highcharter website data preparation")   )   response <- jsonlite::read_json(temp)   if (     length(response) != 2L ||       is.null(response[[1]]$pages) ||       response[[1]]$pages != 1L   ) {     stop("Unexpected or paginated World Bank response: ", url)   }   response }  prepare_home_data <- function(   world,   start_year = 2005L ) {   current_year <- as.integer(format(Sys.Date(), "%Y"))   indicators <- c(     population = "SP.POP.TOTL",     life = "SP.DYN.LE00.IN",     income = "NY.GDP.PCAP.PP.KD",     urban = "SP.URB.TOTL.IN.ZS",     exports = "TX.VAL.MRCH.CD.WT",     imports = "TM.VAL.MRCH.CD.WT"   )   geography <- fetch_wdi("country/all?format=json&per_page=400")   economy_rows <- Filter(     function(x) x$region$value != "Aggregates",     geography[[2]]   )   economies <- data.frame(     iso3 = vapply(economy_rows, function(x) x$id, character(1)),     name = vapply(economy_rows, function(x) x$name, character(1))   )   features <- world$objects$default$geometries   continents <- data.frame(     iso3 = vapply(features, function(x) x$properties[["iso-a3"]], character(1)),     continent = vapply(       features,       function(x) x$properties$continent,       character(1)     )   )   continents <- continents[!duplicated(continents$iso3), ]   # Natural Earth's "Seven seas" group is not a continent. Keep these island   # economies in the same six-region cohort used by every homepage panel.   island_regions <- c(MDV = "Asia", MUS = "Africa", SYC = "Africa")   for (iso3 in names(island_regions)) {     continents$continent[continents$iso3 == iso3] <- island_regions[[iso3]]   }   economies <- merge(economies, continents, by = "iso3")    panels <- list()   source_dates <- list()   for (variable in names(indicators)) {     indicator <- indicators[[variable]]     years <- if (variable == "exports") {       seq.int(start_year, current_year)     } else {       seq.int(current_year - 3L, current_year)     }     # Short ranges avoid slow, very large indicator responses from the API.     ranges <- split(years, ceiling(seq_along(years) / 5L))     responses <- lapply(ranges, function(range) {       period <- paste0(min(range), ":", max(range))       path <- paste0(         "country/all/indicator/",         indicator,         "?source=2&format=json&date=",         period,         "&per_page=20000"       )       fetch_wdi(path)     })     rows <- unlist(lapply(responses, `[[`, 2L), recursive = FALSE)     panel <- data.frame(       iso3 = vapply(rows, function(x) x$countryiso3code, character(1)),       year = as.integer(vapply(rows, function(x) x$date, character(1))),       value = vapply(         rows,         function(x) if (is.null(x$value)) NA_real_ else x$value,         numeric(1)       )     )     names(panel)[3] <- variable     panels[[variable]] <- panel     source_dates[[variable]] <- responses[[1]][[1]]$lastupdated   }   wide <- Reduce(     function(x, y) merge(x, y, by = c("iso3", "year"), all = TRUE),     panels   )   country_panel <- merge(wide, economies, by = "iso3")   coverage <- lapply(     sort(       unique(country_panel$year[country_panel$year >= current_year - 3L]),       decreasing = TRUE     ),     function(year) {       rows <- country_panel[country_panel$year == year, ]       valid <- stats::complete.cases(rows[names(indicators)]) &         rows$income > 0 &         rows$population > 0 &         rows$exports > 0 &         rows$imports > 0       data.frame(         year = year,         economies = sum(valid),         population = sum(rows$population[valid])       )     }   )   coverage <- do.call(rbind, coverage)   candidates <- coverage[coverage$economies >= 150L, ]   if (!nrow(candidates)) {     stop("No recent year has adequate comparable coverage.")   }   year <- max(candidates$year)   snapshot <- country_panel[country_panel$year == year, ]   snapshot <- snapshot[stats::complete.cases(snapshot[names(indicators)]), ]   snapshot <- snapshot[     snapshot$income > 0 &       snapshot$population > 0 &       snapshot$exports > 0 &       snapshot$imports > 0,   ]   history <- country_panel[     country_panel$year <= year,     c("iso3", "year", "exports")   ]   complete_history <- vapply(     split(history, history$iso3),     function(x) {       nrow(x) == year - start_year + 1L && all(is.finite(x$exports))     },     logical(1)   )   snapshot <- snapshot[     snapshot$iso3 %in% names(complete_history)[complete_history],   ]   history <- history[history$iso3 %in% snapshot$iso3, ]   snapshot$gdp <- snapshot$income * snapshot$population   snapshot$exports_pc <- snapshot$exports / snapshot$population   snapshot$imports_pc <- snapshot$imports / snapshot$population   snapshot$trade_balance <- 100 *     (snapshot$exports - snapshot$imports) /     (snapshot$exports + snapshot$imports)   rownames(snapshot) <- NULL   message(     "Selected ",     year,     ": ",     nrow(snapshot),     " economies; Russia included: ",     "RUS" %in% snapshot$iso3   )   world_population <- panels$population$population[     panels$population$iso3 == "WLD" & panels$population$year == year   ]   metadata <- list(     schema_version = 3L,     year = year,     start_year = start_year,     economies = nrow(snapshot),     prepared = as.character(Sys.Date()),     source = "World Bank WDI, source 2",     indicators = as.list(indicators),     source_updated = source_dates,     coverage = coverage,     world_population_coverage = sum(snapshot$population) / world_population,     excluded = setdiff(economies$iso3, snapshot$iso3),     units = list(       income = "PPP, constant 2021 international dollars per person",       exports = "Current US dollars",       imports = "Current US dollars",       exports_pc = "Current US dollars per person",       imports_pc = "Current US dollars per person",       trade_balance = "100 * (exports - imports) / (exports + imports)",       urban = "Percent of population"     )   )   list(countries = snapshot, history = history, metadata = metadata) }  world <- readRDS(system.file(   "maps/custom/world.topo.rds",   package = "highcharter",   mustWork = TRUE )) home_data <- prepare_home_data(world) countries <- home_data$countries metadata <- home_data$metadata

title: From data to charts
text: Give region color every chart. panels use hcrt theme, soft grids small italic captions aligned bottom right. scatter export history share margins plot areas remain aligned grid. article homepage use player. article, chart controls. homepage, one set controls advances four charts.
code: year <- metadata$year regions <- c(   "Africa",   "Asia",   "Europe",   "North America",   "South America",   "Oceania" ) colors <- c("#47475c", "#508CC8", "#F49952", "#61BC7B", "#6699a1", "#9C9EDB") names(colors) <- regions stopifnot(all(countries$continent %in% regions)) region_id <- c(   "africa",   "asia",   "europe",   "north-america",   "south-america",   "oceania" ) names(region_id) <- regions countries <- countries[   order(match(countries$continent, regions), countries$iso3), ] countries$color <- unname(colors[countries$continent]) focus_regions <- "South America" south_america <- countries[countries$continent %in% focus_regions, ] history <- merge(   home_data$history,   countries[c("iso3", "continent")],   by = "iso3" ) trade <- aggregate(exports ~ code: library(highcharter) library(dplyr)  data(penguins, package = "palmerpenguins") data(diamonds, economics_long, package = "ggplot2")  hchart(   penguins,   "scatter",   hcaes(x = body_mass_g, y = flipper_length_mm, group = species) ) penguins2 <- penguins |>   count(species, island) |>   glimpse() ## Rows: 5 ## Columns: 3 ## $ species <fct> Adelie, Adelie, Adelie, Chinstrap, Gentoo ## $ island  <fct> Biscoe, Dream, Torgersen, Dream, Biscoe ## $ n       <int> 44, 56, 52, 68, 124 hchart(penguins2, "column", hcaes(x = island, y = n, group = species)) economics_long2 <- economics_long |>   filter(variable %in% c("pop", "uempmed", "unemploy"))  hchart(economics_long2, "line", hcaes(x = date, y = value01, group = variable))

title: Maps
text: Click South America, 12 countries explore administrative divisions. example, Chile opens 16 regions. Use breadcrumbs return one level jump back continents. clickable point drilldown ID matching child series. three levels use geographic coordinates projection. mapZooming = TRUE, view zooms toward selection series changes. geometry bundled article, click works offline.
code: atlas <- jsonlite::read_json("data/drilldown-south-america.json.gz") atlas$cl <- readRDS(system.file("maps/cl.rds", package = "highcharter")) codes <- setdiff(names(atlas), c("continents", "south_america")) countries <- data.frame(code = codes, value = 1, drilldown = codes)  divisions <- lapply(codes, function(code) {   list(     id = code,     name = atlas[[code]]$title,     type = "map",     mapData = atlas[[code]],     colorAxis = FALSE,     nullColor = "rgba(57,131,113,0.35)",     nullInteraction = TRUE   ) }) continents <- data.frame(code = "sa", value = 1, drilldown = "countries") south_america <- list(   id = "countries",   name = "South America",   type = "map",   mapData = atlas$south_america,   data = list_parse(countries),   joinBy = c("hc-key", "code") )  hcmap(   atlas$continents,   data = continents,   value = "value",   joinBy = c("hc-key", "code"),   name = "Continents" ) |>   hc_mapView(projection = list(name = "EqualEarth")) |>   hc_plotOptions(map = list(nullColor = "rgba(106,120,124,0.16)")) |>   hc_colorAxis(     visible = FALSE,     dataClasses = list(list(from = 1, to = 1, color = "rgba(24,124,101,0.62)"))   ) |>   hc_drilldown(     mapZooming = TRUE,     animation = list(duration = 650),     series = c(list(south_america), divisions)   ) |>   hc_title(text = "Explore administrative divisions") |>   hc_tooltip(     headerFormat = "",     pointFormat = "{point.name}",     nullFormat = "{point.name}"   )

what: Overlay point locations and a vector field
title: Maps
text: mappoint places airports longitude latitude. geographic vector field, flowmap draws arrow two coordinate pairs. example places simulated tornado lower Paraná, near Río de la Plata. footprint enlarged rotation visible regional scale. Arrow length shows relative speed. airports geographic reference points.
code: # fmt: skip airports <- tibble::tribble(   ~name,                     ~code, ~lon,   ~lat,   "Rosario",                 "ROS", -60.79, -32.90,   "Buenos Aires Aeroparque", "AEP", -58.42, -34.56,   "Buenos Aires Ezeiza",     "EZE", -58.54, -34.82,   "Montevideo Carrasco",     "MVD", -56.03, -34.84 )  wind <- data.frame(   radius = rep(c(0.32, 0.65, 0.98), c(6, 12, 18)),   angle = 2 * pi * c((0:5) / 6, (0:11) / 12, (0:17) / 18) ) wind <- wind |>   mutate(     east = cos(angle),     north = sin(angle),     lon = -59.65 + radius * east / cos(-33.85 * pi / 180),     lat = -33.85 + radius * north,     speed = 1 - 0.6 * radius   )  arrows <- with(   wind,   Map(     function(lon, lat, east, north, speed) {       list(         from = c(lon, lat),         to = c(           lon + 0.36 * speed * (north - 0.25 * east) / cos(lat * pi / 180),           lat - 0.36 * speed * (east + 0.25 * north)         )       )     },     lon,     lat,     east,     north,     speed   ) ) hcmap(   atlas$ar,   nullColor = "rgba(106,120,124,0.12)",   borderColor = "#ACB8B5",   showInLegend = FALSE ) |>   hc_add_series(     type = "map",     mapData = atlas$uy,     nullColor = "rgba(106,120,124,0.12)",     borderColor = "#ACB8B5",     showInLegend = FALSE   ) |>   hc_mapView(     projection = list(name = "WebMercator"),     fitToGeometry = list(       type = "MultiPoint",       coordinates = list(c(-61.45, -35.25), c(-55.55, -32.55))     )   ) |>   hc_add_series(     data = arrows,     type = "flowmap",     name = "Simulated wind",     color = "#237469",     fillOpacity = 0.9,     width = 1.6,     markerEnd = list(width = 3, height = 6),     curveFactor = 0,     enableMouseTracking = FALSE   ) |>   hc_add_series(     data = airports,     type = "mappoint",     name = "Airports",     hcaes(lon = lon, lat = lat, name = name),     color = "#934426",     marker = list(symbol = "circle", radius = 3),     dataLabels = list(enabled = TRUE, format = "{point.code}")   ) |>   hc_title(text = "A simulated wind field over the lower Paraná") |>   hc_tooltip(headerFormat = "", pointFormat = "{point.name} ({point.code})") |>   hc_mapNavigation(enabled = TRUE, enableMouseWheelZoom = FALSE)

title: Modules & plugins
text: plugin created Ignacio Vazquez (https://github.com/phpepe) let add regression series existing series chart. Calculates r-squared value (coefficient determination) optionally prints legend. Linear Polynomial regression selected, can print equation legend. Even can get regression series/group. detail parameter can found github page plugin: https://github.com/streamlinesocial/highcharts-regression#regression-settings.
code: library(highcharter)  data(penguins, package = "palmerpenguins")  penguins <- penguins[complete.cases(penguins), ]  hchart(   penguins,   "scatter",   name = "Penguins",   # opacity = 0.35,   hcaes(x = flipper_length_mm, y = bill_length_mm),   regression = TRUE,   regressionSettings = list(     type = "polynomial",     dashStyle = "ShortDash",     color = "skyblue",     order = 3,     lineWidth = 5,     name = "%eq | r2: %r",     hideInLegend = FALSE   ) ) |>   hc_add_dependency("plugins/highcharts-regression.js") hchart(   penguins,   "scatter",   hcaes(x = flipper_length_mm, y = bill_length_mm, group = species),   regression = TRUE ) |>   hc_colors(c("#d35400", "#2980b9", "#2ecc71")) |>   hc_add_dependency("plugins/highcharts-regression.js")

title: Modules & plugins
text: Motion community plugin Lars Cabrera, official Highcharts module. JavaScript ships separately R package; hc_motion() attaches chart. part shared Highcharts bundle. Watch life expectancy change across continents 1952 2007. point carries sequence population-weighted means local Gapminder data. fixed value scale makes changes comparable. Press Play drag year slider; chart begins 1952.
code: library(dplyr)  data(gapminder, package = "gapminder")  history <- gapminder |>   group_by(continent, year) |>   summarise(lifeExp = weighted.mean(lifeExp, pop), .groups = "drop")  years <- sort(unique(history$year)) points <- history |>   arrange(continent, year) |>   group_by(name = as.character(continent)) |>   summarise(y = first(lifeExp), sequence = list(lifeExp), .groups = "drop")  highchart() |>   hc_chart(type = "bar", spacingBottom = 88) |>   hc_title(text = "Longer lives, different trajectories") |>   hc_subtitle(text = "Population-weighted life expectancy by continent") |>   hc_xAxis(categories = points$name) |>   hc_yAxis(     min = 25,     max = 85,     title = list(text = "Life expectancy (years)")   ) |>   hc_add_series(     name = "Life expectancy",     data = list_parse(points),     colorByPoint = TRUE   ) |>   hc_tooltip(valueDecimals = 1, valueSuffix = " years") |>   hc_motion(     labels = as.character(years),     startIndex = 0,     magnet = list(step = 1),     updateInterval = 900   ) |>   hc_credits(enabled = TRUE, position = list(y = -65)) |>   hc_caption(     text = "Source: Gapminder. The continent means are weighted by population."   ) |>   hc_size(height = 460)

what: Price and carat across nine panels
title: Multiple axes
text: Compare price (US dollars) weight (carats) three cuts three colors ggplot2::diamonds. panel shows reproducible sample 100 diamonds. panels share axis limits.
code: library(dplyr) library(purrr)  set.seed(42) groups <- ggplot2::diamonds |>   filter(     cut %in% c("Very Good", "Premium", "Ideal"),     color %in% c("D", "E", "F")   ) |>   group_by(color, cut) |>   slice_sample(n = 100)  keys <- group_keys(groups) panels <- map(seq_len(nrow(keys)), function(i) {   list(     left = paste0(35 * ((i - 1) %% 3), "%"),     top = paste0(35 * ((i - 1) %/% 3), "%"),     width = "27%",     height = "22%",     offset = 0,     startOnTick = FALSE,     endOnTick = FALSE   ) }) x_axes <- map2(panels, seq_along(panels), function(panel, i) {   c(     panel,     list(       min = 0,       max = ceiling(max(groups$carat)),       title = list(text = paste(keys$cut[i], "·", keys$color[i]))     )   ) }) y_axes <- map(panels, function(panel) {   c(     panel,     list(       min = 0,       max = 20000,       tickPositions = c(0, 10000, 20000),       title = list(text = NULL)     )   ) })  chart <- highchart(height = 780) |>   hc_title(text = "Diamond price by carat") |>   hc_subtitle(     text = "Columns show cut. Rows show color. Prices in US dollars."   ) |>   hc_chart(alignTicks = FALSE) |>   hc_xAxis(x_axes) |>   hc_yAxis(y_axes) |>   hc_legend(enabled = FALSE)  reduce2(   group_split(groups),   seq_along(panels),   function(hc, rows, i) {     hc_add_series(       hc,       rows,       "scatter",       hcaes(x = carat, y = price),       name = paste(keys$cut[i], keys$color[i]),       xAxis = i - 1L,       yAxis = i - 1L,       marker = list(radius = 2)     )   },   .init = chart )

title: Shiny applications

code: library(shiny) library(highcharter)  ui <- fluidPage(   theme = bslib::bs_theme(version = 5),   style = "max-width: 48rem;",   selectInput("measure", "Iris measurements", c("Sepal", "Petal")),   highchartOutput("flowers", height = "310px") )  server <- function(input, output, session) {   output$flowers <- renderHighchart({     hchart(       iris,       "scatter",       hcaes_string(         x = paste0(input$measure, ".Length"),         y = paste0(input$measure, ".Width"),         group = "Species"       )     ) |>       hc_xAxis(title = list(text = "Length (cm)")) |>       hc_yAxis(title = list(text = "Width (cm)"))   }) }  shinyApp(ui, server)

title: Shiny applications
text: original proxy playground inspired three examples. tab creates chart , uses highchartProxy() change chart already screen. Series. Compare monthly temperatures Santiago Tokyo. Toggle Tokyo add remove series. Switch daily means daily highs replace data series ID hcpxy_set_data(). single hcpxy_redraw() displays changes. Try comparison polar axes. Points. Add remove month observed air traffic. Turn dashed forecast repeat last twelve observations one year ahead. forecast moves observations, even switch columns. Layout. Rearrange 592 students grid, semicircle circle. hcpxy_update_series() changes item layout preserving counts. Open app tab switch weekly daily Stock prices visible date range narrows, run Stock proxy app read Stock walkthrough.
code: library(shiny) library(bslib) library(highcharter)  hc_set_theme("hcrt") palette <- hc_theme("hcrt")$colors  weather <- aggregate(   cbind(temp_mean, temp_max) ~ city + month,   transform(city_weather, month = as.integer(format(date, "%m")) - 1L),   mean ) city_months <- function(city, measure) {   rows <- weather[weather$city == city, ]   data.frame(x = rows$month, y = round(rows[[measure]], 1)) }  counts <- as.numeric(AirPassengers) months <- seq(   as.Date("1949-01-01"),   by = "month",   length.out = length(counts) + 12L ) dates <- datetime_to_timestamp(months) traffic <- data.frame(x = dates[seq_along(counts)], y = counts) initial <- 24L # A seasonal naive forecast repeats the last 12 observed months. outlook <- function(n) {   data.frame(x = dates[n + seq_len(12L)], y = counts[(n - 11L):n]) }  eyes <- as.data.frame.table(   margin.table(HairEyeColor, 2),   responseName = "students" )  ui <- page_fluid(   title = "Proxy playground",   theme = bs_theme(     version = 5,     primary = palette[1],     base_font = c("IBM Plex Sans", "sans-serif"),     heading_font = c("Alegreya Sans SC", "sans-serif")   ),   style = "max-width: 48rem;",   tags$main(     class = "py-2",     navset_underline(       nav_panel(         "Series",         div(           class = "d-flex align-items-center flex-wrap gap-3 pt-3",           selectInput(             "measure",             "Monthly average of",             c("Daily mean" = "temp_mean", "Daily high" = "temp_max"),             width = "11rem"           ),           checkboxInput("tokyo", "Compare with Tokyo", TRUE, width = "auto"),           checkboxInput("polar", "Polar chart", width = "auto")         ),         highchartOutput("weather", height = "320px")       ),       nav_panel(         "Points",         div(           class = "d-flex align-items-center flex-wrap gap-2 py-3",           actionButton("add", "Add a month", class = "btn-primary"),           actionButton("remove", "Remove last month"),           checkboxInput("forecast", "Show seasonal forecast", width = "auto")         ),         radioButtons(           "type",           "Observed series",           c("Line" = "line", "Columns" = "column"),           inline = TRUE         ),         highchartOutput("passengers", height = "300px")       ),       nav_panel(         "Layout",         div(           class = "pt-3",           radioButtons(             "shape",             "Arrange the dots",             c("Grid", "Semicircle", "Circle"),             inline = TRUE           )         ),         highchartOutput("students", height = "320px")       )     )   ) )  server <- function(input, output, session) {   output$weather <- renderHighchart({     highchart() |>       hc_title(text = "City temperatures, 2025") |>       hc_xAxis(categories = month.abb) |>       hc_yAxis(         title = list(text = ""),         labels = list(format = "{value}°C"),         tickInterval = 10       ) |>       hc_tooltip(shared = TRUE, valueSuffix = " °C", valueDecimals = 1) |>       hc_add_series(         city_months("Santiago", "temp_mean"),         "line",         hcaes(x, y),         id = "Santiago",         name = "Santiago",         color = palette[1]       ) |>       hc_add_series(         city_months("Tokyo", "temp_mean"),         "line",         hcaes(x, y),         id = "Tokyo",         name = "Tokyo",         color = palette[3]       )   })    weather_proxy <- highchartProxy("weather", session)   observeEvent(     input$tokyo,     {       if (input$tokyo) {         hcpxy_add_series(           weather_proxy,           city_months("Tokyo", input$measure),           "line",           hcaes(x, y),           id = "Tokyo",           name = "Tokyo",           color = palette[3]         )       } else {         hcpxy_remove_series(weather_proxy, "Tokyo")       }     },     ignoreInit = TRUE   )   observeEvent(     input$measure,     {       cities <- c("Santiago", if (input$tokyo) "Tokyo")       for (city in cities) {         hcpxy_set_data(           weather_proxy,           "line",           city_months(city, input$measure),           hcaes(x, y),           id = city         )       }       hcpxy_redraw(weather_proxy)     },     ignoreInit = TRUE   )   observeEvent(     input$polar,     {       hcpxy_update(weather_proxy, chart = list(polar = input$polar))     },     ignoreInit = TRUE   )    output$passengers <- renderHighchart({     hchart(       traffic[seq_len(initial), ],       "line",       hcaes(x, y),       id = "traffic",       name = "Observed",       showInLegend = TRUE     ) |>       hc_title(text = "International air passengers") |>       hc_xAxis(type = "datetime", title = list(text = "")) |>       hc_yAxis(title = list(text = "Passengers (thousands)")) |>       hc_tooltip(xDateFormat = "%B %Y", valueDecimals = 0, valueSuffix = "k")   })    passengers <- highchartProxy("passengers", session)   last <- reactiveVal(initial)   observeEvent(input$add, {     n <- last() + 1L     req(n <= length(counts))     hcpxy_add_point(       passengers,       "traffic",       point = list(x = dates[n], y = counts[n])     )     last(n)   })   observeEvent(input$remove, {     n <- last()     req(n > 12L)     hcpxy_remove_point(passengers, "traffic", i = n - 1L)     last(n - 1L)   })   observeEvent(     input$type,     {       hcpxy_update_series(passengers, "traffic", type = input$type)     },     ignoreInit = TRUE   )   observeEvent(     input$forecast,     {       if (input$forecast) {         hcpxy_add_series(           passengers,           outlook(last()),           "line",           hcaes(x, y),           id = "outlook",           name = "Seasonal forecast",           linkedTo = "traffic",           dashStyle = "ShortDash",           color = palette[3],           showInLegend = TRUE         )       } else {         hcpxy_remove_series(passengers, "outlook")       }     },     ignoreInit = TRUE   )   observeEvent(     last(),     {       n <- last()       updateActionButton(session, "add", disabled = n == length(counts))       updateActionButton(session, "remove", disabled = n == 12L)       if (input$forecast) {         hcpxy_set_data(           passengers,           "line",           outlook(n),           hcaes(x, y),           id = "outlook",           redraw = TRUE         )       }     },     ignoreInit = TRUE   )    output$students <- renderHighchart({     hchart(       eyes,       "item",       hcaes(name = Eye, y = students),       id = "eyes",       name = "Students",       showInLegend = TRUE,       dataLabels = list(enabled = FALSE)     ) |>       hc_title(text = "Eye color of 592 students") |>       hc_subtitle(text = "Each dot represents one student.") |>       hc_colors(c("#80583B", "#508CC8", "#AE965E", "#57936A")) |>       hc_legend(labelFormat = "{name} · {y}") |>       hc_tooltip(pointFormat = "{point.y} students")   })   observeEvent(     input$shape,     {       angles <- switch(         input$shape,         Grid = list(NULL, NULL),         Semicircle = c(-90, 90),         Circle = c(0, 360)       )       semicircle <- input$shape == "Semicircle"       highchartProxy("students", session) |>         hcpxy_update_series(           "eyes",           startAngle = angles[[1]],           endAngle = angles[[2]],           center = c("50%", if (semicircle) "88%" else "50%"),           size = if (semicircle) "160%" else "90%"         )     },     ignoreInit = TRUE   ) }  shinyApp(ui, server)

title: Shiny applications
text: lit segment adds 1 dB band’s gain, starting −12 dB. Hover band, click , drag top release . event readout. drag mouseOver values refresh every 150 ms. drop value shows final gain soon release band. Open app tab Point clicks arrive automatically input$eq_point_click. Register mouseOver, drag drop hc_add_event_point() receive inputs . example, input$eq_point_mouseOver$pointid identifies band pointer input$eq_point_drag$y gives gain drag.
code: library(shiny) library(highcharter)  bands <- data.frame(   band = c("60 Hz", "250 Hz", "1 kHz", "4 kHz", "16 kHz"),   gain = c(0, 5, -4, 8, 2) ) events <- c("click", "drag", "mouseOver", "drop")  ui <- fluidPage(   theme = bslib::bs_theme(version = 5),   style = "max-width: 48rem;",   tags$head(tags$style(     "     #eq .highcharts-grid-line { pointer-events: none; }     #readings { font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; }     #readings .recalculating { opacity: 1; }   "   )),   tags$main(     h2("Equalizer"),     p("Hover or click a band. Drag its top to change the gain."),     highchartOutput("eq", height = "320px"),     h3("Latest event by type"),     tags$dl(       id = "readings",       class = "row row-cols-2 row-cols-sm-4",       lapply(events, function(event) {         div(           class = "col",           tags$dt(event),           tags$dd(textOutput(event, inline = TRUE))         )       })     )   ) )  server <- function(input, output, session) {   output$eq <- renderHighchart({     hchart(       bands,       "column",       hcaes(x = band, y = gain, id = band),       name = "Gain",       color = "#39d9f5",       zIndex = 1,       cursor = "ns-resize",       dragDrop = list(         draggableY = TRUE,         dragMinY = -12,         dragMaxY = 12,         dragPrecisionY = 1       )     ) |>       hc_add_series(         type = "column",         name = "Band range",         data = rep(12, nrow(bands)),         color = "#203245",         enableMouseTracking = FALSE,         accessibility = list(enabled = FALSE),         zIndex = 0       ) |>       hc_plotOptions(         column = list(           grouping = FALSE,           threshold = -12,           borderWidth = 0,           borderRadius = 0,           maxPointWidth = 54,           minPointLength = 4         )       ) |>       hc_chart(backgroundColor = "#101a29") |>       hc_legend(enabled = FALSE) |>       hc_xAxis(         title = list(text = NULL),         gridLineWidth = 0,         labels = list(style = list(color = "#e4ecf4"))       ) |>       hc_yAxis(         min = -12,         max = 12,         tickInterval = 1,         labels = list(step = 6, style = list(color = "#e4ecf4")),         title = list(text = "Gain (dB)", style = list(color = "#e4ecf4")),         gridLineColor = "#101a29",         gridLineWidth = 2,         gridZIndex = 4       ) |>       hc_tooltip(valueSuffix = " dB", valueDecimals = 0) |>       hc_add_event_point(event = "mouseOver") |>       hc_add_event_point(event = "drag") |>       hc_add_event_point(event = "drop")   })    lapply(events, function(event) {     point <- reactive(input[[paste0("eq_point_", event)]])     reading <- if (event %in% c("drag", "mouseOver")) {       throttle(point, 150)     } else {       point     }     output[[event]] <- renderText({       value <- reading()       if (is.null(value)) {         return("—")       }       sprintf("%s · %+d dB", value$pointid, as.integer(value$y))     })   }) }  shinyApp(ui, server)

title: Shiny applications
text: dotplot shows mean petal length species, rounded nearest millimeter. colorByPoint = TRUE, species gets color. Pause species 200 ms click immediate selection. detail shows petal length width 50 flowers color. Shiny proxy updates detail points, series color title keeping axes fixed comparison. Open app tab run example local checkout, load package open app directory: original Shiny examples also include population explorer linked views.
code: library(shiny) library(highcharter)  species <- aggregate(Petal.Length ~ Species, iris, mean) species$mean_mm <- round(10 * species$Petal.Length) colors <- setNames(   hc_theme("hcrt")$colors[seq_len(nrow(species))],   species$Species )  ui <- fluidPage(   theme = bslib::bs_theme(version = 5),   style = "max-width: 60rem;",   tags$main(     p(       "Each dot represents 1 mm of mean petal length.",       "Hover or click a species to see its 50 flowers in the same color."     ),     fluidRow(       column(         5,         div(           class = "mx-auto",           style = "max-width: 24rem;",           highchartOutput("overview", height = "295px")         )       ),       column(7, highchartOutput("detail", height = "295px"))     )   ) )  server <- function(input, output, session) {   output$overview <- renderHighchart({     hchart(       species,       "dotplot",       hcaes(x = Species, y = mean_mm, id = Species),       name = "Mean petal length",       colorByPoint = TRUE,       slotsPerBar = 3,       itemPadding = 0.1,       cursor = "pointer"     ) |>       hc_chart(inverted = TRUE) |>       hc_colors(unname(colors)) |>       hc_xAxis(title = list(text = NULL)) |>       hc_yAxis(min = 0, title = list(text = "Mean petal length (mm)")) |>       hc_tooltip(valueDecimals = 0, valueSuffix = " mm") |>       hc_add_event_point(event = "mouseOver")   })    initial <- as.character(species$Species[1])   requested <- reactiveVal(initial)   selected <- reactiveVal(initial)   settled <- debounce(requested, 200)   observeEvent(settled(), selected(settled()), ignoreInit = TRUE)   observeEvent(     input$overview_point_mouseOver,     requested(input$overview_point_mouseOver$pointid)   ) title: Showcase
text: 27 March 2004, Hurricane Catarina approached southern Brazil. snapshot shows ERA5 wind 10 m 18:00 UTC. arrow points downwind color gives speed. Sampling 0.25° reanalysis every 0.75° keeps circulation legible scale. Hover arrow speed bearing. Copernicus ERA5 · NASA satellite image Catarina.
code: wind <- read.csv(system.file(   "extdata",   "catarina-wind.csv",   package = "highcharter" )) wind$speed <- sqrt(wind$u^2 + wind$v^2) wind$bearing <- (atan2(wind$u, wind$v) * 180 / pi + 360) %% 360  # Draw each arrow in local east/north coordinates, then convert to longitude/latitude. arrows <- lapply(seq_len(nrow(wind)), function(i) {   cell <- wind[i, ]   angle <- cell$bearing * pi / 180   along <- c(-0.24, 0.24, 0.08, 0.24, 0.08)   across <- c(0, 0, -0.09, 0, 0.09)   east <- along * sin(angle) + across * cos(angle)   north <- along * cos(angle) - across * sin(angle)   coordinates <- Map(     c,     cell$lon + east / cos(cell$lat * pi / 180),     cell$lat + north   )   list(     value = cell$speed,     bearing = cell$bearing,     lon = cell$lon,     lat = cell$lat,     geometry = list(type = "LineString", coordinates = coordinates)   ) })  hcmap(   "custom/world.topo.json",   nullColor = "#f0eee8",   borderColor = "#a8b1af",   showInLegend = FALSE,   enableMouseTracking = FALSE ) |>   hc_chart(plotBackgroundColor = "#eaf3f6") |>   hc_mapView(     projection = list(name = "WebMercator"),     padding = 0,     fitToGeometry = list(       type = "MultiPoint",       coordinates = list(c(-56, -33.5), c(-40.5, -22.75))     )   ) |>   hc_add_series(     type = "mapline",     name = "10 m wind",     data = arrows,     colorKey = "value",     lineWidth = 2,     tooltip = list(       pointFormat = "{point.lat:.1f}°, {point.lon:.1f}° · {point.value:.1f} m/s towards {point.bearing:.0f}°"     )   ) |>   hc_colorAxis(     min = 0,     max = 15,     tickPositions = c(0, 3, 6, 9, 12, 15),     stops = color_stops(colors = c("#497991", "#137b78", "#c87b21", "#a63742"))   ) |>   hc_legend(     layout = "horizontal",     align = "center",     title = list(text = "Wind speed (m/s)")   ) |>   hc_add_series(     type = "mappoint",     name = "Coastal cities",     showInLegend = FALSE,     color = "#45434a",     marker = list(radius = 2),     data = list(       list(name = "Florianópolis", lon = -48.55, lat = -27.60),       list(name = "Porto Alegre", lon = -51.23, lat = -30.03)     ),     dataLabels = list(       enabled = TRUE,       format = "{point.name}",       align = "right",       style = list(fontSize = "10px", fontWeight = "normal")     )   ) |>   hc_caption(     text = "Wind: Copernicus Climate Change Service (ERA5), sampled at 0.75°."   ) |>   hc_title(text = "Catarina off the coast of Brazil") |>   hc_subtitle(text = "Surface wind · 27 March 2004, 18:00 UTC") |>   hc_size(height = 500)

code: library(highcharter) library(shiny)  snapshot <- read.csv(system.file(   "extdata",   "spy-2025.csv",   package = "highcharter" )) daily <- data.frame(day = as.Date(snapshot$date), close = snapshot$SPY.Close) weekly <- daily[!duplicated(cut(daily$day, "week"), fromLast = TRUE), ]  ui <- fluidPage(   theme = bslib::bs_theme(version = 5),   style = "max-width: 48rem;",   p(     "View up to six weeks for daily closing prices. Zoom out to see weekly closes."   ),   actionButton("april", "Explore April"),   highchartOutput("prices") )  server <- function(input, output, session) {   output$prices <- renderHighchart({     highchart(type = "stock") |>       hc_title(text = "SPY closing price, 2025") |>       hc_legend(enabled = TRUE) |>       hc_xAxis(         id = "days",         ordinal = FALSE,         minRange = 7 * 86400000,         events = list(           afterSetExtremes = JS(             "function (e) {               if (e.trigger !== 'updatedData') {                 Shiny.setInputValue('prices_range', [e.min, e.max]);               }             }"           )         )       ) |>       hc_navigator(adaptToUpdatedData = FALSE) |>       hc_rangeSelector(         selected = 1,         buttons = list(           list(type = "month", count = 1, text = "1m"),           list(type = "all", text = "All")         )       ) |>       hc_add_series(         weekly,         "line",         hcaes(day, close),         id = "closing",         name = "Weekly close",         dataGrouping = list(enabled = FALSE)       ) |>       hc_tooltip(valueDecimals = 2, valuePrefix = "$")   })    observeEvent(input$april, {     highchartProxy("prices", session) |>       hcpxy_set_extremes(         as.Date("2025-04-01"),         as.Date("2025-04-30"),         axis = "days"       )   })    observeEvent(input$prices_range, {     days <- as.Date(       unlist(input$prices_range) / 86400000,       origin = "1970-01-01"     )     detail <- as.numeric(diff(days)) <= 42     prices <- if (detail) {       subset(daily, day >= days[1] & day <= days[2])     } else {       weekly     }     highchartProxy("prices", session) |>       hcpxy_set_data("line", prices, hcaes(day, close), id = "closing") |>       hcpxy_update_series(         id = "closing",         name = if (detail) "Daily close" else "Weekly close"       )   }) }  shinyApp(ui, server)

what: Price, moving averages, volume and momentum
title: Stock charts and Stock Tools

code: snapshot <- read.csv(system.file(   "extdata",   "spy-2025.csv",   package = "highcharter" )) SPY <- xts::xts(snapshot[-1], order.by = base::as.Date(snapshot$date)) SPY <- quantmod::adjustOHLC(SPY, use.Adjusted = TRUE) close <- quantmod::Cl(SPY) fast_mean <- TTR::SMA(close, n = 5) slow_mean <- TTR::SMA(close, n = 100) momentum <- TTR::RSI(close, n = 14) sell_level <- xts::xts(rep(70, NROW(SPY)), order.by = time(SPY)) buy_level <- xts::xts(rep(30, NROW(SPY)), order.by = time(SPY))  highchart(type = "stock") |>   hc_rangeSelector(selected = 1) |>   hc_title(text = "SPY: price, volume and momentum in 2025") |>   hc_yAxis(create_axis(3, heights = c(3, 1, 1), turnopposite = TRUE)) |>   hc_add_series(SPY, yAxis = 0, name = "SPY", id = "instrument") |>   hc_add_series(fast_mean, yAxis = 0, name = "5-day mean") |>   hc_add_series(slow_mean, yAxis = 0, name = "100-day mean") |>   hc_add_series(     quantmod::Vo(SPY),     yAxis = 1,     name = "Volume",     type = "column"   ) |>   hc_add_series(momentum, yAxis = 2, name = "RSI (14)") |>   hc_add_series(     sell_level,     yAxis = 2,     name = "RSI 70",     dashStyle = "ShortDash",     color = "#94A3B8",     lineWidth = 1,     showInLegend = FALSE,     enableMouseTracking = FALSE   ) |>   hc_add_series(     buy_level,     yAxis = 2,     name = "RSI 30",     dashStyle = "ShortDash",     color = "#94A3B8",     lineWidth = 1,     showInLegend = FALSE,     enableMouseTracking = FALSE   ) |>   hc_yAxis(title = list(text = "Price")) |>   hc_tooltip(valueDecimals = 2, shared = TRUE) |>   hc_size(height = 720)

x <- c("Income:", "Genre", "Runtime") y <- c( "$ {point.y}", "{point.series.options.extra.genre}", "{point.series.options.extra.runtime}" ) tooltip_table(x, y) #> [1] "
Income: $ {point.y}
Genre {point.series.options.extra.genre}
Runtime {point.series.options.extra.runtime}
"

Stock Tools now loads indicators embeds toolbar icons self-contained HTML widgets vignettes. Stock Tools can add technical indicators another widget renders re-renders page (#595). Data-frame heatmaps position dates times either axis accept omitted coordinates. Date cells span one day. Date-time cells use shortest observed interval axis, one second single time. Set colsize rowsize choose different interval milliseconds. Multivariate forecasts plot predictions intervals series shared separate axes. legend toggles confidence level across panels. Shiny proxies now send zero messages series add, remove update, points update. Forecast charts use time index predictions intervals. Series frequencies 1, 4 12 use numeric axis. data_to_sankey() counts transitions consecutive columns, skips links missing endpoints assigns unique link IDs. Numeric binning handles missing values tied quantiles. Inputs fewer two columns return empty link table. Axes one category now display label axis tooltips, including category numeric (#395, #438). hchart(data, type = "gantt") selects native Gantt constructor data frames, preserving task rows, date axes dependency links. Supplying new rules list hc_responsive() replaces previous rules. Circle-presets preserve rectangular heatmap cells. hcrt theme uses IBM Plex Sans credits. French, Norwegian Bokmål Simplified Chinese use official Highcharts language packs. Japanese Korean use AI-generated translations. hcmap() accepts already loaded GeoJSON list without downloading map data. Network charts preserve current theme hiding coordinate axes. reflow enabled, charts fill available widget width height Viewer standalone browser, including resizing.
